No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **40** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 1047fe10166c943807d61218e2fde9c3ab22e502` → `packageMentionDocs`.

```sh

git fetch origin d93878c5d29f897f3b1604e008b846aec064fd22 && git checkout d93878c5d29f897f3b1604e008b846aec064fd22
```

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `4da89b8eae37cd6a71817c78f61a866d65c99d52`

Isolated at-tier review. Judged against the diff at that head (8 files, 3 commits), the card's own comments (the option-B ruling `5695555178`, the unlock `5731154376`), and the governing text re-read on `origin/main` at `aadea24b8` — ADR-0131 D5 plus its 2026-09-17 amendment, #11663 design comment `5394453215` (P5, Choice 4, §5 steps 6–7, row L5), #16682 comment `5587754690` (Choice 4A). The PR body and the dev report were read but nothing below is taken from them.

### ① Derived judgments

Every change to the accept/reject set and to the published surface that the diff produces, one by one:

1. **Walled derivation narrowed (correct).** `resolve-authz-context.ts` §6b: the one line that sets `hasPlatformAdminGrant` from an unscoped `admin_full_access` grant gains `and not legacyGrantAnchorRetired`, where `legacyGrantAnchorRetired = postureEnforcesWall(resolveTenancyPosture())`. Read on `origin/main`, not from the body: `postureEnforcesWall(p)` is `p !== 'single'` (`packages/spec/src/security/tenancy-posture.ts:53`); `resolveTenancyPosture()` returns `OS_TENANCY_POSTURE` when set (throwing on an invalid value), else `isolated` when `OS_MULTI_ORG_ENABLED` is truthy, else `single` (`packages/types/src/env.ts:147`). So on `group`/`isolated` — including a rig that is walled only through the legacy multi-org flag — the row stops conferring the `PLATFORM_ADMIN` rung, the built-in `platform_admin` position (§6c reads `hasPlatformAdminGrant`) and the rung consumers. The set's own name and capabilities are still pushed onto `grants.permissions` on every posture, so the change is to standing only. That is exactly the scope the ruling and the amended D5 name.
2. **The `else if (hasPlatformAdminGrant)` arm removed (correct, no accept/reject effect).** Its body was solely the posture-keyed pointer; under `single` it was already a no-op (#13667), so the removal changes no derivation output on any posture. `hasPlatformAdminGrant = true` is still set in the config branch; §6c and §6d are untouched.
3. **`single` is genuinely untouched — derived from the diff, not asserted.** Under `single` the gate evaluates false and the §6b line is behaviour-identical to base; the removed arm was inert there; `hasPlatformAdminStanding` (`resolve-authz-context.ts:1127`) is a projection of `resolveUserAuthzGrants` reading the rung, so plugin-auth's session payload, impersonation and sso-register gates (`auth-manager.ts` `isPlatformAdminUserId`) move with the derivation by construction and cannot fork per posture. Boot side: the four hunks in `bootstrap-platform-admin.ts` are the header, the import block and the walled branch; the `single` early return (`not walled and unscopedHolder` ⇒ `already_have_admin`) and the `single` promotion are untouched. One caution the diff introduces: `resolveTenancyPosture()` is now read once per `resolveUserAuthzGrants` call instead of only inside the retired arm; it is an environment read (the branch's own multiset pin measures zero added queries) and the same value is already validated at boot, so I do not count it.
4. **Boot path (log-only).** The `sys_user` read that fed the pointer is gone (one fewer boot read for a walled legacy holder); the undeclared-config `error` line is no longer skipped when a legacy holder exists and gains a conditional sentence naming the row and the holder's user id. `reason` values and the return shape are unchanged. Judged in ③.
5. **Two names leave the published entry (correct, and verified on the built artefact).** `packages/core/package.json` `exports` has exactly `.` and `./logger`; `src/index.ts:44` is `export *` from `./security/index.js`; `security/index.ts` drops both names. Across the whole PR-head tree the two names occur in zero non-comment source lines (the hits are comments and the two absence pins; positive control on the same grep: `matchesConfiguredPlatformAdmin` resolves at its definition and its re-export). Built artefact: I extracted the head with `git archive` into an isolated scratch copy (the shared checkout was never touched), ran an offline install and `turbo run build --filter=@objectstack/core` (4 tasks, exit 0), and read `packages/core/dist`: `index.d.ts` / `index.js` / `index.cjs` contain `reportLegacyPlatformAdminGrant` 0 / 0 / 0 and `resetLegacyPlatformAdminGrantReport` 0 / 0 / 0, with positive controls on the same files `matchesConfiguredPlatformAdmin` 4 / 3 / 4 and `setPlatformAdminConfigSink` 2 / 2 / 3, and negative control `notAnExport_xyz` 0 / 0 / 0. A runtime probe of `dist/index.js` answers `false` for both removed names, `true` (function) for `matchesConfiguredPlatformAdmin`, `setPlatformAdminConfigSink` and `hasPlatformAdminStanding`, `false` for the negative control. CI `Build Core` and `Type Check · workspace` are `success` on this head, so no in-repo TypeScript importer survives.
6. **The same two names also leave two more published entries — undeclared.** `packages/runtime/src/index.ts:247` and `packages/plugins/plugin-hono-server/src/adapter.ts:4` are `export * from '@objectstack/core'` (hono's `src/index.ts:5` re-exports the adapter). Both packages are non-private and their built `dist/index.d.ts` carry that `export *` statement verbatim on line 2 (read on a sibling built tree at `19dda8c94`, which predates this branch; on that instrument the name grep returns 0 for the removed names and 0 for the kept control alike, which is what a re-export statement looks like, so the statement is the evidence, not the count). Consequence: `@objectstack/runtime` and `@objectstack/plugin-hono-server` lose the two names from their published surface too. Carried to ②.
7. **Widening: none.** No new export, no new key on any published payload (the bootstrap return shape is unchanged; a longer log string is not a key), no newly accepted input. The only additions are a module-private const, comments, and tests.
8. **Test double (`structuredClone` of the recorded `where`)** is test-only; the committed batch-equivalence golden is not in the diff. Correct.

🔴 **Finding — the walled retirement is done at one of the two readers of the same anchor.** `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/last-admin-guard.ts` enumerates platform administrators from the same unscoped, in-window `admin_full_access` grant row (grade 1, its lines ≈900–950) with no posture read anywhere in the file (0 occurrences of `postureEnforcesWall` / `resolveTenancyPosture`; control on the same instrument: `auth-plugin.ts` has 7). Its own header binds it to the derivation: 「the same evidence `resolveAuthzContext` derives `platform_admin` from」, 「the enumeration must answer the SAME question `resolveAuthzContext` does」; design P6 says the admin-standing surface moves with the derivation, and L2 is the precedent — it added the config anchor to §6b and to this guard's grade 3 in the same leg. After this diff, on a walled rig that still holds a legacy row (the row is deliberately left in place and pinned so), the guard counts a holder the derivation no longer recognises. Consequence, stated abstractly: a write that ends the last config-anchored administrator's standing is permitted because the guard believes an administrator remains, and the deployment is then without a platform administrator — the outcome the guard exists to refuse; conversely a write that removes the now-inert row is refused with a message claiming it would remove the last administrator. The guard's own pin `last-admin-guard.config-anchor.test.ts:257` (「ALLOWS it when the same user also holds the legacy grant」) encodes the pre-L5 model, and no guard test runs under a walled posture (0 hits for `OS_TENANCY_POSTURE` / `OS_MULTI_ORG_ENABLED` across `last-admin-guard*.test.ts`; control: `bootstrap-platform-admin-walled-owner.test.ts` has 21), so CI green here measures `single` only. The PR body, the report's deviations and its out-of-scope findings do not mention the guard. This is a derivation/enumeration dual-track opened on walled rigs by the diff — the class the migration window was built to close — and it is undeclared. Recoverable by a configuration change, which is why it is one finding and not a lockout without remedy; it is still a finding. Lesser, same family: `packages/core/src/security/admin-standing-surface.ts:130–135` (inside the touched surface) still declares the unscoped grant as 「the grant that makes a user a platform admin」 with no posture qualifier; the gate compares that declaration's column set, which is unchanged, so the gate is right and the `reason` prose is what is now stale.

### ② Semver level

Convention read from `scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs` on `origin/main`, not assumed: during the launch window a breaking change ships `minor`, never `major`; the bump level is explicitly not the carrier — the BREAKING banner in the changeset body and an ADR-0087 disposition marker are; and a Clause-② PR must grade at least one package whose published source it moves `minor` or above. The changeset grades `@objectstack/core` and `@objectstack/plugin-security` `minor`, opens with a BREAKING banner, and carries exactly one `adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription)` marker whose category is right (no Zod schema, no `packages/spec` declaration, no stored representation; the compiler and the boot log are the reaching channels). The `Clause-②` line lives on the PR body and the card's claim comment, which is where `check-clause2-carriers` reads it; 0 of the ≈40 breaking-shaped changesets on `origin/main` carry one in the body, so its absence from the changeset is the convention, not a miss. **Level: correct on both packages named.** `@objectstack/plugin-security`'s own change is behavioural (boot log), with `bootstrapPlatformAdmin`'s return contract unchanged; `minor` under the same banner is the right grade.

**Naming: incomplete on a strict reading.** Per ① item 6 the removed names also leave `@objectstack/runtime` and `@objectstack/plugin-hono-server`. All 70 publishable packages sit in one `fixed` group, so the bump is identical whatever is named and the level is unaffected — but during the window the changeset is also the CHANGELOG tombstone an upgrading consumer greps, and neither of those packages' CHANGELOG will carry it. Precedent is mixed: `PluginSecurityScanner`'s removal was declared on core only (core CHANGELOG 4 hits, runtime 0), `ApiRegistry`'s named all three. Recorded as a gap to close cheaply (add the two packages, or state in the changeset why they are not named); not the verdict driver.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Fail-closed boot line no longer skipped — mechanically forced, not scope creep.** L4's skip rested on two premises the diff itself removes: the row confers, and the pointer carries the remedy. With the pointer gone and the row inert under a wall, the unskipped `error` line is the only word such a rig gets on the paths that reach the bootstrap without plugin-auth's init refusal (`auth-plugin.ts:550` still refuses boot for walled + undeclared, so the backstop matters for `os meta resync` and embeddings). Leaving the skip would ship the silent half of a fail-closed guard. The added holder sentence is conditional (pinned with a control) and names a user id at `error` level, which the retired pointer already did. Correct call.
- **`PlatformAdminConfigSink.warn` left in place — correct call.** The interface is published; dropping `warn` narrows a published type and breaks every object-literal caller, a third removal the card did not authorise. Its TSDoc (「Sink for the refusal notice」) remains accurate for `error`. Noted in acceptance notes, which is what Prime Directive #10 asks for something that is neither a defect nor a contract violation.
- **`ADR-0131` and `packages/spec` untouched — correct.** The D5 text on `origin/main` says what the diff does (walled half and both symbols on 17.x; the row's ownership unchanged, C3/v18). The diff writes, deletes and re-owns no row; that boundary is pinned.
- **`docs/qa/platform-checklist/areas/access-security.json:2462` and `:2492` — the note is not enough.** The clause instructs a runner, with a log oracle, to expect a pointer the runtime no longer emits on any posture and standing a walled rig no longer confers; the anchor parenthetical names a deleted symbol. Outside the dispatch surface, but a checklist item that now specifies retired behaviour is a contract-text drift a `checklist-test` run will red on, and 「noted, not filed」 leaves no carrier. Same for `content/docs/permissions/authorization.mdx:113–118`, which states that `PLATFORM_ADMIN` derives from 「two anchors, either of which is sufficient」 with no posture qualifier — true under `single`, false under a wall after this diff (the docs-drift bot flagged the page). Both need a filed card (the L7 docs leg is the natural home). Not verdict-driving alone.
- **Not flagged by the author, and should have been:** the `last-admin-guard` sibling reader (① finding) and the two re-export republishers (②).

**Verdict reasoning.** The diff does what the ruling authorises, keeps `single` intact — verified, not assumed — and removes the two symbols cleanly from the built artefact with controls. It fails on one thing: it retires the walled anchor at the derivation while leaving the lockout guard counting that anchor on the same rigs, undeclared. Two routes to green, the owning seat's choice: (a) posture-key the guard's grade-1 enumeration the same way §6b is keyed (plugin-auth already imports both helpers) and pin it under a walled posture in both directions; or (b) if the guard is ruled its own sequenced leg, say so in the PR body and file the card before landing. Alongside, add `@objectstack/runtime` and `@objectstack/plugin-hono-server` to the changeset (or state why not), and file the checklist/docs drift.

Reviewed-by: `session_019hBqDVrwbijUCoK9qsss2E`
